title: Audit telemetry minification & redaction patterns — ops draft
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc captures a practical approach to (1) minifying and redacting audit telemetry before SIEM export to limit PII and token costs, (2) strategies for event sampling/sharding for long-tail high-volume endpoints, and (3) RBAC v2 considerations that affect evidence provenance and reversible transformations. The target audience is SRE/Infra, Security, and Product teams working on evidence automation and SIEM export pipelines.

Background / motivation:
- We’re seeing sustained growth in tokenized audit payloads (model prompts + outputs) that blow up storage and SIEM costs.
- Legal/regulatory needs require both fidelity (for forensics) and minimization (for privacy).
- RBAC v2 introduces richer actor metadata (service identities, subroles) which changes redaction boundaries — some callers are allowed to see more fields.

High-level design principles (guiding constraints):
1) Preserve forensic linkability: every minified payload must contain a stable event_id, timestamp, and cryptographic evidence pointer (e.g., evidence_sha256) so we can fetch the full record from cold storage when authorized.
2) Deterministic reversible redaction (when permitted): for enterprise customers, we prefer reversible encryption of sensitive fields stored in a tenant-specific KMS envelope, rather than brittle irreversible hashing.
3) Least privilege at export: SIEM exports should only include fields permitted by the destination’s RBAC tier and legal region.
4) Cost-first heuristics: aggressively compress and sample high-cardinality fields (e.g., raw_prompt, model_tokens) while preserving statistical signals for quality monitoring.

Proposed minification pipeline (per-event):
- Stage 0: classification (fast classifier tags a payload as: high-sensitivity | moderate | low). Classifier input: route_id, user_role, presence_of_prompt, contains_attachment. Implementation: simple rules + probabilistic model for unknown routes.
- Stage 1: canonicalize schema (normalize keys to audit.v2.* names, ensure timestamp format ISO-8601 with tz).
- Stage 2: field-level policy application: apply per-field policy table (keep | truncate | redact | encrypt | sample). See policy table section below.
- Stage 3: token-aware truncation for prompts/response: keep first 256 chars + fingerprint suffix (sha256 of full prompt). Optionally gzip then base64-encode for cold storage link.
- Stage 4: enrichment & provenance: attach event_id, route_version, server_region, k8s_pod (if SRE=allowed), evidence_pointer (cold storage object id), and a small deterministic bloom filter for quick matching (optional).
- Stage 5: export adapter: map to SIEM schema (Splunk/Hunter/Elastic). Include an export metadata wrapper: {export_time, exporter_id, policy_version, rbactier}.

Field-level policy table (working draft):
- user.email: redact unless destination has customer-PII access (RBAC allow-list). Redaction: reversible envelope via customer KMS (format: ENCv1:kid:base64). Fallback: sha256 as a non-reversible digest.
- user.id: keep stable id (uuid) but truncate prefix if cross-tenant; i.e., tenant_hash:user_suffix. Purpose: maintain linkability without leaking tenant global ids.
- prompt_text / response_text: default = truncate(256) + prompt_fingerprint; high-sensitivity routes -> encrypt to cold storage only, SIEM receives placeholder.
- model_name & model_variant: keep (important for ops).
- api_key_id: redact completely in SIEM; export only api_key_meta (tier, owner_role).
- session_kv_cache_keys: sample at 0.1% and include only hashed keys to detect cache churn patterns.
- ip.address: for EEA orgs = anonymize (mask last octet); for US = retain -> depends on export region policy.
- stack_trace / exception.message: keep but scrub file paths and absolute user names.

RBAC v2 interactions (non-obvious cases):
- Role-scoped redaction rules: RBAC v2 supports role hierarchies and subroles. The exporter must evaluate "effective redaction policy" by intersecting event sensitivity label with actor's allowed disclosures. Example: event labeled sensitive_user_content but actor service_role=security:incident-response may be allowed to retrieve full payload via evidence retrieval API.
- Service accounts vs human users: treat service principals as lower-privilege by default unless explicitly granted. Add a flag in event: actor.is_service_principal = true/false.
- Attribute-based exceptions: customers may request PII retention for certain routes by contract. Exporter should attach contract_id when exception applies and route export to a sealed pipeline.

Sampling & sharding patterns for high volume endpoints:
- Use stratified sampling: keep 100% of errors and timeouts; sample successes by route and token count buckets. Example strata: {errors:100%, latency>1s:50%, token>4096:10%, token 1024-4096:1%}.
- Adaptive telemetry throttle: monitor SIEM forward queue occupancy and auto-scale down sample rates for low-value strata.
- Identify heavy hitters: maintain per-route counters and when a route crosses threshold (e.g., 1M events/day), switch to inline minification + cold-store-only storage for full payloads.

Evidence automation hooks (for retrieval & auditability):
- evidence_pointer format: cloud://audit-archive/<tenant>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/events/<event_id>.gz.enc
- retrieval API must validate: caller identity, RBAC policy, request purpose, and time-bounded consent. Log retrieval attempts as distinct audit events.
- retention policy tags: sticky_retention_days (tenant policy), legal_hold=true|false. When legal_hold=true, do not purge even if TTL expired; mark for separate legal team workflow.

SIEM export mapping (notes):
- Flattened envelope fields to export: [event_id, ts, tenant_id_safe, route_id, severity, outcome, model_name, truncated_prompt, prompt_fp, event_class, exporter_id, policy_version]
- Never export raw_prompt or raw_response unless exporter flagged with allow-list via RBAC and contract.
- Include an export_version field to help downstream parsers evolve (we expect v1, v2, v3 mappings across time).

Versioning & migration plan (v1 -> v3 scope):
- v1 (baseline): lightweight minification (truncate prompts), basic field policies, deterministic event_id and evidence_pointer. SIEM exports include minimal envelope.
- v2 (rbac-aware): incorporate RBAC v2 decision engine at export-time, reversible encryption option, enriched provenance fields, sampling policies.
- v3 (policy-driven at scale): per-tenant policy runtime, adaptive sampling, legal_hold integration, and cooperative retention with cold storage lifecycle APIs.
- Migration notes: keep export_version and policy_version in every exported record. Provide a fallback parser for v1-v2-v3 in SIEM ingestion (server-side remapper).

Operational runbook (quick):
- Q: SIEM shows unexplained drop in events for route X after policy bump.
  Steps: check exporter logs -> policy_version applied -> sampling table -> evidence_pointer spikes -> cold store errors -> rollback policy if necessary.
- Q: Customer requests full payload for an incident.
  Steps: verify contract_id & RBAC permission, issue retrieval request (LR-REQ-xxxxx), log retrieval audit event, fetch from cold store via KMS unwrap, deliver to authorized recipient, then log delivery.

Open questions & TODOs (team action items):
- [ ] Finalize reversible encryption envelope format (ENCv1 spec) and KMS integration pattern (SSE vs CSE). (owner: Daniel)
- [ ] Build a lightweight classifier prototype for sensitivity labeling and measure false-positive rate on sample of last 30 days of telemetry. (owner: Lara)
- [ ] Define canonical policy table schema (YAML/JSON) and an admin UI for contracts/exceptions. (owner: Owen)
- [ ] Add retention/legal_hold signals into cold store lifecycle manager and test purge workflows.

References & notes:
- See GH PR above for early exporter adapter code (WIP).
- SEC-3421 contains compliance requirements per EEA PII handling.
- We'll align event_id format with loglineage v0.1 recommendations from the audit team (note: cross-reference audit-event-id guidelines doc).

Quick appendix: sample exported envelope (illustrative, not exact):
{
  "export_version": "v1",
  "exporter_id": "audit-exporter-02",
  "event_id": "evt-20250218-7a3e",
  "ts": "2025-02-18T14:22:09Z",
  "tenant_id_safe": "t-7f3a",
  "route_id": "chat-completion.v2",
  "severity": "info",
  "outcome": "success",
  "model_name": "open-llama-13b-q8",
  "truncated_prompt": "Customer asked for status update...",
  "prompt_fp": "sha256:abc123...",
  "policy_version": "policy-2025-02-10",
  "rbac_tier": "enterprise-observability"
}

---
Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally practical—ops checklist + clear delegation. We will split into two follow-ups: (A) technical spec for exporter adapters (with code snippets and libraries), (B) legal/compliance mapping doc (contract exceptions, EEA/US mapping).
